key_insight: APEX-SWE is a practical benchmark that measures whether frontier AI models can perform economically valuable, real-world software engineering work by evaluating end-to-end, system-level tasks rather than narrow micro-tasks.
problem_solved: Current evaluations focus on small, well-defined tasks that do not reflect the long-horizon, heterogeneous responsibilities of real software engineers; APEX-SWE fills this gap by introducing tasks that mirror actual integration and system-engineering work.
method: Define two novel task classes that reflect real-world software engineering workflows, including Integration tasks (n=100) that require building end-to-end systems across cloud primitives, business apps, and infrastructure.
Design benchmark exercises that capture long-horizon, multi-step decision making and end-to-end execution rather than isolated code snippets or unit problems.
Provide standardized evaluation criteria emphasizing economic value, robustness, and cross-component correctness to assess model utility for industry software engineering.
impact: APEX-SWE helps practitioners and organizations understand which models can deliver real engineering value (not just code completion), guiding model selection, tooling, and deployment for production software workflows.
visual_elements: High-level diagram showing an AI model orchestrating cloud primitives, business apps, and infra to deliver an end-to-end integration task
Bar chart or heatmap comparing model performance on narrow benchmarks vs. APEX-SWE (illustrating gap)
Flowchart of a long-horizon task broken into multi-step sub-tasks (design → integrate → test → deploy)
Icon set representing economic value metrics: time saved, deployment success, bug reduction, and cross-system compatibility
paper_authors: Abhi Kottamasu, Akul Datta, Aakash Barthwal, Chirag Mahapatra, Ajay Arun
